title: Scholarships - Financial Aid
lines: Scholarships are a type of financial aid that does not have to be repaid. Sources for scholarships include federal and state governments, the university, your academic department or professional school, community and civic groups, and private industry.
Coordination of Scholarships with Other Financial Aid

Scholarships do not increase the total amount of your need-based financial aid. In most cases, they will change the composition of your financial aid package. Outside scholarships will typically reduce the amounts of student loans or Federal Work-Study you may receive. We make every attempt to preserve any university need-based grants. Each situation must be reviewed in light of the availability of funds, state and federal regulations, and the university’s financial aid policies.
For more information on how outside scholarships are coordinated with your financial aid, please view our “ How Financial Aid Works ” video and fast-forward to approximately the six-minute mark.
If your scholarship agency requires you to submit proof of enrollment, you can provide a USC Enrollment and Fee Summary by printing a copy of it from your myUSC student profile.

Federal regulations require that we consider all your resources when determining your eligibility for financial aid. If you are a recipient of an outside award not listed in your financial aid summary, please send us a copy of your scholarship award notification so that we can adjust your financial aid package accordingly and notify you of the revision.

Your scholarship will be added to your financial aid summary shortly after we receive your notification, but funds will not be disbursed until the scholarship check is received. For checks mailed to us by the agency or by the student, please allow three weeks from the mailing date for processing. Allow about one week for checks dropped off in person.
Most scholarships will replace some type of financial aid in your aid summary. If you would like to know how your scholarship will affect your financial aid eligibility, please contact our office.

USC Scholarships are administered consistent with the University’s Notice of Non-Discrimination. Recipients are chosen without regard to race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, or any other prohibited characteristic.
USC administers more than a dozen prestigious scholarship programs awarded based on academic excellence, leadership, service and talent.
Search this Scholarship Management portal for departmental awards or see if your department maintains its own scholarship website. Contact your department for details.
The Office of the Provost maintains this database of internal and external awards and fellowships.
Athletic scholarships are awarded based on recommendations from the Athletics Department. Please visit our Athletic Awards page for more information.

Some departments provide their scholarships in the form of a monthly stipend that is paid directly to the award recipient. Stipend payments are made monthly according to the university’s stipend schedule.
